title: Captain's Compass
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4ac43b71fc2f205193b2e2f00b1fc01e985b2a03.png)An 8-point compass rose, commons.wikimedia.org

"Ahoy mateys! Arrr... We pirates look for sunken treasure. Which direction we sail?"

"Shiver me timbers!"   The pirate captain is a superstitious *sea-dog* and only likes to sail in the exact directions of an 8-point compass rose: north (N), south (S), east (E), west (W), north-east (NE), south-east (SE), north-west (NW) and south-west (SW).

"Arrr!"  So you *scallywags* need to come up with a list of directions for the captain to follow, in order to go from one $(x,y)$ point in the sea to another $(x,y)$ point while traversing the least possible distance. Only the directions are necessary; the captain is no *landlubber* and will figure out how long to go in each direction. The captain sails a positive distance in every direction you list.

For example, if the ship is at (2,1) and the treasure is at (6,8), we can tell the captain to first sail N to (2,4) then NE to the treasure traversing the least possible distance. It would be possible to arrive by first going E to (6,1) then N: but this is not a shortest path.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3df76f9f9a30ae421295cc1fbc1ce787459d53c0.png)Illustration for sample 1. N then NE is a shortest path. E then N is not.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with two integers $x_s$ and $y_s$ ($-5400 \leq x_s,y_s \leq 5400$), the starting position of the ship.
- One line with two integers $x_t$ and $y_t$ ($-5400 \leq x_t,y_t \leq 5400$), the position of sunken treasure.

We have $(x_s,y_s) \neq (x_t,y_t)$.

## Output

Output the directions that the captain should follow to reach the sunken treasure while traversing the least possible distance. Each direction should be one of: "`N`", "`S`", "`E`", "`W`", "`NE`", "`SE`", "`SW`", "`NW`".

If there are multiple valid solutions, you may output any one of them.
